items.title: Flames fall to Avalanche after Makar’s four-assist night
items.body: DENVER — Artturi Lehkonen scored twice, Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and an assist, and the Colorado Avalanche beat the Calgary Flames 5-2 on Saturday night. Martin Necas and Brock Nelson also scored, and defenceman Cale Makar had four assists for the Avalanche. Mackenzie Blackwood made 25 saves. Colorado has won two in a row against opponents playing on the second night of a back-to-back. The Avalanche defeated New Jersey on Wednesday and faced Calgary’s No. 3 goaltender, Arsenii Sergeev , less than 24 hours after the Flames beat Seattle. Joel Farabee and Martin Pospisil scored for Calgary. Sergeev made 29 saves in his second career start and first this season. Sergeev was recalled from the AHL when the Flames placed Devin Cooley on the injured list with a lower-body injury. Colorado was not whistled for a penalty, while Calgary took three — two on a double-minor late in the third period. The Avalanche, who lost defenceman Josh Manson for two months after he injured an ankle against the Devils, saw Nelson exit in the second when he took a shot by Makar off the side of his helmet. Nelson, who scored earlier in the period, was able to skate to the bench and down the tunnel. He returned in the third period. Nelson capped a three-goal burst in the first 10 minutes of the second that gave Colorado a 4-0 lead. Farabee scored 1:43 after Nelson’s goal, and Pospisil made it 4-2 when he scored 1:59 into the third. Lehkonen deflected Makar’s shot from the point at 4:09 to make it 5-2. Two of Blackwood's stops came after MacKinnon made it 1-0 late in the first. Blackwood made a sprawling glove save on Matt Coronato with 8.5 seconds left in the period and then stopped Farabee 12 seconds into the second.

items.title: Canadiens’ Evans among veterans stepping up in Suzuki’s absence
items.summary: What Jake Evans has provided in Nick Suzuki’s absence is worth highlighting, especially considering the standard he’s set for his Canadiens teammates. Eric Engels explains how Saturday’s win showcased the impact Montreal’s veterans have made without their captain.
items.body: MONTREAL — Straight stats, no fancy stuff, here’s what Jake Evans has provided the Montreal Canadiens in Nick Suzuki’s five-game absence: two goals, three assists, a plus-11 rating, and a 55.4 per cent face-off efficiency while averaging 17:04 per game. Next-man-up stuff, indeed. Worth highlighting, no doubt. Especially considering Evans normally plays as Montreal's fourth-line centre but has elevated to set the standard for the maturity the young Canadiens are exhibiting night after night without their captain. “It’s like he always makes the right play,” said Chris Kreider after Evans made enough right plays to notch an assist, win 11 of 16 draws, and finish with a plus-4 rating in a 5-4 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins Saturday. It was Montreal’s fifth straight win since Suzuki went down with a hand injury. They had two-goal leads in the third period in all five games and executed on the details to win all five in regulation thanks to veterans like the 30-year-old Evans setting the example for players like 22-year-old Owen Beck . Phillip Danault , who played his 800 th NHL game Saturday, is another who’s been doing that. The 33-year-old has been playing close to 20 minutes a night in Suzuki’s absence but not playing any differently than he would playing 16 minutes per game from his usual (lower) slot. items.body: Goalie’ spot in NHL, shutout on Hockey Fights Cancer ‘culmination of a long journey’ BOSTON -- The idea of a shutout started to creep in, late in the third period. Michael DiPietro had fought so long and so hard to even get to this point, to gain a foothold in an NHL that had seemed constantly just out of reach, but now, with his first NHL win in the books, his first NHL shutout seemed possible. There it was, he thought. His mom was giving him a helping hand. As DiPietro said later, “Definitely a good, friendly bounce there, and it wasn’t just by happenstance.” Back home, in Amherstburg, Ontario, the idea was much the same. Assunta Fenty-DiPietro, Michael’s stepmom, was going through her usual game routine -- “basically 9,000 heart attacks,” as his dad, Vic, put it -- when she connected those same dots. “She’s like, ‘That’s Rebecca, I know it,’ she says. ‘Not tonight!’” Vic DiPietro said. “She was jumping three feet in the air and the whole nine yards.” It wasn’t until that morning, Oct. 22, that DiPietro had put it all together. He arrived at TD Garden, knowing that he was getting the start that evening against the Nashville Predators, his third of the season. items.title: Canucks starting to deliver on effort, competitiveness despite loss
items.summary: Nobody promised wins. But the Vancouver Canucks are finally starting to deliver on the effort and competitiveness they pledged as a baseline.
items.body: VANCOUVER – Nobody promised wins. But the Vancouver Canucks are finally starting to deliver on the effort and competitiveness they pledged as a baseline. Their 4-2 loss Saturday to the Toronto Maple Leafs dropped the Canucks to 3-12-1, which is grotesque and worse than anyone expected even for the start of a National Hockey League rebuild. But they had their goalie out and pressing for a late tying goal, as they did in Thursday’s 3-2 road loss to the San Jose Sharks, and the Canucks didn’t drown at five-on-five against another superstar-driven team. And even though Vancouver’s poor middle period decided the game, the two shots that allowed Toronto to go ahead 3-1 could have been handled better by goalie Leevi Merilainen. After getting outshot in 12 of their first 13 games, which included a 10-game losing streak, the Canucks have now narrowly outshot their opponents in three straight contests. Shots on Saturday were 29-28. It is sobering that these last three games, a 6-5 overtime win against the Anaheim Ducks on Tuesday followed by the goalie-out losses against the Sharks and Leafs, probably constitute a “hot streak” at this stage for the NHL’s worst team. But at least there is progress, which was difficult to find through most of October – a month that was Halloween for the Canucks from start to finish. “Getting closer,” coach Manny Malhotra said Saturday night. “It's not close to where we need to be or need to get to, but there is progress there. It's frustrating as we talk about these games after loss after loss, but we do see improvement in different areas of our game. It's just... tough to see those when there's no correlation to wins.” “Obviously, the end result has to change somehow,” Canucks winger Paul Cotter , part of an effective fourth line, told Sportsnet.

items.body: Tanev returns for Maple Leafs; Perron plays first game for Stars; Cooley week to week for Flames Welcome to the NHL Status Report. Here is the latest lineup/injury news around the NHL. Ivan Provorov made his season debut for the Blue Jackets in a 3-1 loss against the Dallas Stars on Saturday and had one shot on goal in 19:31. The defenseman sustained a lower-body injury and was placed on injured reserve Oct 1. Provorov, who missed the first 11 games of the season, had never missed a game due to injury in his 10-season NHL career. He had played 778 games, including 375 in a row, and only missed three games due to COVID protocol in 2022. "Give him a chance to get his feet wet," Columbus coach Rick Bowness said. "He's dying to play. If there's one guy that can play without practicing for a couple weeks, it's him. He's been working his butt off. He said he felt better now than he did in training camp." Provorov had 31 points (nine goals, 22 assists) in 82 games last season and averaged 24:49 of ice time per game. Chris Tanev was activated from injured reserve by the Maple Leafs on Saturday and returned in a 4-2 win against the Vancouver Canucks, playing 19:21. The defenseman practiced fully with teammates in a regular jersey at the morning skate Wednesday but did not play in a 5-4 loss at the Seattle Kraken. Tanev was injured in the first period of a 6-3 win against the Colorado Avalanche on Oct. 10 and missed nine games. items.title: Kucherov would consider trade to Maple Leafs or Canadiens
items.body: The reigning MVP could have his eyes on the Atlantic Division. The Toronto Maple Leafs and Montreal Canadiens are two teams that Nikita Kucherov would consider as trade destinations, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported during Saturday Night Hockey . Kucherov has a modified no-trade clause, meaning he can submit a list of 10 approved teams he can be traded to. The Russian forward has a 10-team list, but the teams on it are currently unknown, Friedman added. This latest development comes after Kucherov informed both his teammates and the Lightning organization that he will not be re-signing with Tampa Bay and would like to be traded. There was a meeting between Kucherov, his agent Dan Milstein, head coach Jon Cooper, and GM Julien Brisebois on Friday, but they were unable to settle the situation, Friedman reported. The Lightning released a statement saying they would not be trading Kucherov. "We are aware of the media reports regarding the future of Nikita Kucherov with the Lightning," Brisebois said in a statement. "We unequivocally have no intention of trading Nikita." Kucherov, 33, is in the final season of an eight-year, $76-million contract and had 130 points (44 goals, 86 assists) last season in his second Hart Trophy-winning campaign. Friedman's reporting also included that Kucherov initially wanted his contract to be in the same territory as Kirill Kaprizov's deal, but that changed after Leo Carlsson's off-season offer sheet. However, the biggest catalyst in Kucherov's decision was the lack of pace in the negotiations.

items.body: Another chapter could be coming to the Dylan Larkin saga in Detroit. After making the decision on Thursday to sit out until the Red Wings fulfill his trade request, Larkin might adjust the list of teams that he is willing to waive his no-movement clause for. "He has a 10-team trade list that he's willing to go to," Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman said on the latest Saturday Headlines segment. "I think over the next 24-to-48 hours, it's possible we see that trade list altered." Helene St. James of The Detroit Free Press reported on Oct. 20 that Larkin's trade list includes the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche. When Larkin initially requested a trade out of the Motor City, it was reported that he was only open to a move to the Panthers, Wild and Golden Knights. But now that Larkin has opted out of playing with the Red Wings after scoring two goals and six points over 10 games, the club's former captain appears ready to find a spot outside some of the premier American NHL destinations. "Some teams like Florida and Vegas, even Colorado, it's very hard to see (a trade) happening, if not impossible," Friedman said Saturday. "So, I do think it's possible that Larkin may take some teams off, or possibly even add some teams on." Larkin was suspended without pay and taken off the roster by Detroit after the 30-year-old centre informed the team he would no longer play for the franchise. Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff said Thursday his goal is to acquire players that can help right away, adding he's open to deals for prospects and draft picks that give the franchise a fair return for someone of Larkin's calibre.

items.summary: Sidney Crosby added another honor to his historic career on Saturday night against the Montreal Canadiens.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Sidney Crosby continues to rack up NHL records and milestones. On Saturday, the Pittsburgh Penguins forward surpassed Ray Bourque for the most assists with a single NHL franchise, with a pair of assists in the first two periods against the Montreal Canadiens. The two assists, first on the opening goal to Erik Karlsson, and later on the 2-2 goal to Tommy Novak, brought him to a total of 1,112, passing Bourque’s 1,111. Wayne Gretzky, despite holding the record for the most assists in NHL history with 1,963, posted only 1,086 of those with the Edmonton Oilers , the team he spent the longest with. Rounding out the top five on the all-time assists-with-one-team leaderboard are Steve Yzerman, with 1,063 assists for the Detroit Red Wings , and Mario Lemieux, with 1,033 assists with the Penguins. Crosby’s first Saturday assist came as the primary to Karlsson’s goal, with Novak providing the secondary assist, bringing him to 100 career NHL assists. Meanwhile, Crosby now has 657 goals and 1,112 assists for 1,769 points in 1,433 regular-season games. In addition, Crosby has netted 72 goals and 134 assists for 206 points in 186 Stanley Cup Playoff games. The latest accolade comes in what has already been a history-making season for Crosby. Lining up alongside Kris Letang and Evgeni Malkin, the trio became the longest group of three to play on a single team , hitting 21 consecutive seasons, and amassed the most wins by a trio together, with 494 on Sept. 30. While Crosby’s point total has been slow to come by at 39 years old, with three goals and four assists for seven points in 13 games heading into the matchup with the Canadiens, he will be hoping for an uptick in production as the Penguins continue through the fall. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined Montreal’s Kaiden Guhle impaired Sergei Murashov ’s ability to play his position in the crease prior to Cole Caufield ’s goal . items.title: Penguins’ Sidney Crosby sets NHL record for assists with single franchise
items.body: Sidney Crosby 's Hall of Fame resume grew a little longer on Saturday. With a first-period helper on Erik Karlsson's power-play goal against the Montreal Canadiens, Crosby set the NHL record for assists recorded with a single franchise. The assist was the 1,112th of Crosby career — all of them coming over his 22 seasons with the Pittsburgh Penguins . He surpassed the previous record holder, Ray Bourque, who racked up 1,111 assists over his 21 years playing for the Boston Bruins. With his 1,112 apples, Crosby sits seventh on the all-time NHL leaderboard, 23 behind Paul Coffey. Wayne Gretzky is the career leader at 1,963. Crosby is off to a slow start by his standards in 2026-27, but now has three goals and five assists through the first 14 games of Pittsburgh's season. The 39-year-old has scored at above a point-per-game pace in each year of his career. In 2025-26, the longtime Penguins captain had 74 points (29 goals, 45 assists) in 68 contests.

items.body: LOS ANGELES — Tage Thompson scored twice, including the go-ahead goal with 6:20 remaining, and the Buffalo Sabres beat the Los Angeles Kings 3-2 on Saturday to extend their road point streak to seven games. Jack Quinn had a goal and an assist, Zach Benson and Rasmus Dahlin each had two assists, and the Sabres won their third straight overall. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made 27 saves. Corey Perry had a power-play goal, Andre Lee also scored and Anton Forsberg stopped 28 shots for the Kings. Thompson put the Sabres back in front on a one-timer off a pass from Quinn on a power play at 13:40 of the third period. Buffalo had controlled long stretches of the game before allowing the Kings to get back into it by taking some unnecessary penalties. Buffalo controlled the first period but only led 1-0 on Quinn’s eighth goal when he scored on a power play at 6:35. Even with Los Angeles gaining momentum in the second half of the second period, the Sabres made it 2-0 on Thompson’s ninth with 4:22 left. Perry got the Kings on the board on a power play with 2:36 to go, though they needed a coach’s challenge to overturn a goaltender interference call. Lee tied it 1:29 into the third. The Kings were without top forward Adrian Kempe, who is day to day because of an undisclosed injury. Martin Chromiak made his NHL debut, taking Kempe’s place on the first line and the power play.

items.summary: No update on Howard’s condition was available at the end of the first period after suffering the knee-on-knee hit.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect New York Islanders forward Emil Heineman was ejected from his team’s game on Saturday against the Edmonton Oilers after receiving a five-minute major penalty and game misconduct at 2:22 of the first period. The 24-year-old made knee-on-knee contact with Oilers forward Isaac Howard along the boards in the neutral zone, and Howard was helped off the ice towards the dressing room following the collision. No immediate update on his condition was available. This season, Heineman has two goals and four assists for six points in 13 games, and before Saturday’s brief showing, averaged 15:52 minutes per game. This season marks his second with the Islanders, after previously suiting up for the Montreal Canadiens for four games in 2023-24 and 62 games in 2024-25. Last season, he scored 22 goals and nine assists for 31 points, while playing in each of New York’s 82 games. Should the Swedish forward be assigned any additional suspension, it would mark his first supplemental discipline at the NHL level for in-game action, having only been fined $2,500 for taking his rookie lap without a helmet in 2023. Howard, 22, had one goal and two assists for three points in 12 games with the Oilers heading into Saturday’s matchup, already nearly matching his rookie season output from 2025-26, which saw him net two goals and three assists for five points in 29 NHL games, despite spending most of the season with the Oilers’ AHL affiliate, the Bakersfield Condors. items.title: Matt Pavelich, first linesman in Hockey Hall of Fame, dead at 92
items.body: NEW YORK — Matt Pavelich, the first linesman inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame, has died. He was 92. Pavelich officiated games in 19 consecutive Stanley Cup Finals from 1961-79 as part of his 23 seasons working in the NHL. He took part in 1,727 regular season and 245 playoff games during that stretch before serving as the league's supervisor of officials and going into the Hall in 1987. Commissioner Gary Bettman called Pavelich a true icon of the profession. “No linesman in the history of the National Hockey League was more universally respected nor more widely admired than Matt Pavelich,” Bettman said in a statement. “Pavelich personified professionalism and integrity while possessing a warm personal touch that enabled him to develop working relationships with players and coaches.”

Lightning head coach Jon Cooper, for his part, is doing his best to restore a sense of normalcy for the remainder of the season, at least. items.title: Senators’ Burakovsky, Foegele out three to four weeks
items.summary: Forwards Andre Burakovsky and Warren Foegele are set to miss the next three to four weeks with injuries, head coach Travis Green said before Ottawa’s showdown against the San Jose Sharks on Saturday.
items.body: The Ottawa Senators ' forward depth has taken a hit for the next few weeks. Forwards Andre Burakovsky and Warren Foegele are set to miss the next three to four weeks with injuries, head coach Travis Green said before Ottawa's showdown against the San Jose Sharks on Saturday. Burakovsky suffered a lower-body injury in Friday's game against the Los Angeles Kings. It's unclear how he got hurt, but he logged 4:54 of ice time before being ruled out midway through the second period. The 13-year NHL vet is in his first season with the Senators and has made eight appearances without recording a point. Burakovsky owns a minus-two rating through 88:03 of ice time, with four blocks and three hits in that span. Foegele, meanwhile, was placed on the injured list Friday with a knee injury. He was hurt in Tuesday's game against the Vegas Golden Knights after a knee-on-knee collision with Jeremy Lauzon in the third period. The 30-year-old has had a steady start to his first full season with the Senators after being acquired from the Los Angeles Kings at last year's trade deadline. He has one goal and three assists in 13 games, averaging 12:04 of ice time per night.

items.title: Maple Leafs Activate Chris Tanev Off IR
items.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs have activated defenseman Chris Tanev off injured reserve.
items.body: Register Login Maple Leafs Activate Chris Tanev Off IR By Brian La Rose | at October 31, 2026 12:57 pm The Maple Leafs will welcome back a key veteran defenseman tonight against Vancouver. Chris Tanev has been activated off injured reserve, according to the NHL’s media site, meaning he will be back to take on one of his former teams. Tanev sustained a lower-body injury three weeks ago in Colorado in his sixth game of the season, receiving a week-to-week designation soon after. At the time, the thought was that his designation could last for up to six weeks but he’ll be back in half that time. The 36-year-old is a key shutdown defender for Toronto when he’s in the lineup. The problem is that the oft-injured veteran has been hurt more than he has played over the last two seasons. Tanev was limited to just 11 appearances last season with an injury that required late clearance heading into training camp this year. He’s now missed nine of 15 games in the early going this season. The Maple Leafs enter play tonight as the highest-scoring team in the NHL but sit outside a playoff spot thanks to being in the bottom five league-wide defensively in terms of goals allowed. Tanev should definitely help on the defensive side of things and should also help augment a penalty kill that sits second in the league heading into play today with a 92.3% success rate. Toronto had an active roster spot so no corresponding move needed to be made to bring Tanev onto the roster. He will likely take the place of Dakota Mermis in the lineup, who logged less than 10 minutes in Thursday’s loss against Seattle.

items.title: Opinion: Unlike Hellebuyck And Larkin, Nikita Kucherov Is Doing The Lightning A Solid
items.summary: Nikita Kucherov shocked the NHL by requesting a trade from the Tampa Bay Lightning, but unlike Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin, he is doing his team a solid by doing so.
items.body: James Guillory-Imagn Images James Guillory-Imagn Images Opinion: Unlike Hellebuyck And Larkin, Nikita Kucherov Is Doing The Lightning A Solid Ken Campbell Partner Oct 31, 2026 4:54 PM Published Oct 31, 2026 4:54 PM Nikita Kucherov shocked the NHL by requesting a trade from the Tampa Bay Lightning, but unlike Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin, he is doing his team a solid by doing so. Wow, this one is seismic. Among the superstars in the NHL who are asking/demanding they be moved, there's probably not a person in hockey who had Tampa Bay Lightning star Nikita Kucherov on their bingo card. With 13-plus seasons, two Hart Trophies, two Art Ross Trophies, two Stanley Cups, and more than 1,100 career points as the franchise’s leading scorer, Kucherov looked like as sure a bet as you could find to finish his career with the team that drafted him. More Videos But, unlike Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin, Kucherov is actually doing his team a favor with his public declaration. For so many reasons, this is different than the other two. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images The red, white and blue looks clean, calm and cool heading into one of hockey’s biggest events. On Saturday, USA Hockey revealed the 25-player roster set to represent the United States at the 2026 IIHF Women’s World Championship. Team USA is trotting out 20 of the 23 players who were part of the gold-medal-winning squad at the 2026 Winter Olympics , the team’s first gold at the Winter Games since 2018. The only players who aren’t back on the roster from Milan are Kendall Coyne Schofield, Britta Curl-Salemme and goaltender Ava McNaughton. Coyne Schofield isn’t playing at all this season, as she announced that she’s pregnant with her second child. With so much familiarity throughout the roster, it’s hard not to think the U.S. isn’t on a path to a second consecutive Women’s Worlds gold. Along with Captain America Hilary Knight coming into her record 16th WWC appearance, the U.S. has extensive winning pedigree. Veterans such as Alex Carpenter, Megan Keller and Jesse Compher are all looking to add another medal to their trophy case, while youngsters such as Laila Edwards, Abbey Murphy and Olympic MVP Caroline Harvey look to further solidify themselves as superstars. Goaltending seems to have little holes as well. Aerin Frankel and Gwyneth Philips backstopped the team to the gold at the 2025 WWC and Olympics this past February, with the duo making history in Milan. The one notable difference is the lack of college players. With the Worlds being moved to November, it was expected that some players might not elect to leave campus for the event. items.summary: The Stars signed the veteran Perron earlier this month, who has been getting in shape over the past couple of weeks.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Some reinforcements are coming to the Lone Star State, including an anticipated debut. When speaking to the media at morning skate, Dallas Stars head coach Glen Gulutzan announced that forward David Perron will make his debut on Saturday night, when the Stars take on the Columbus Blue Jackets . He also mentioned that he’s “90 percent” sure that defenseman Esa Lindell will return to the lineup. Perron signed a one-year contract with the Stars on Oct. 16 and has spent the past couple of weeks getting in shape. His deal has a prorated cap hit of $850,000. Perron moves to Dallas hoping to produce a little bit more and stay healthier than he has in the past couple of seasons. After an impressive stretch in which he posted at least 45 points in eight consecutive seasons, the Stanley Cup champion posted only 16 points in 43 games with the Ottawa Senators in 2024-25, improving only slightly to 28 points in 65 appearances last year. He started last season with the Sens before the trade deadline , when he was traded to the Detroit Red Wings , though he did little to improve the team’s postseason chances, scoring just three goals in 16 contests. In 1,239 regular-season games in the NHL, Perron has posted 332 goals and 480 assists for 812 points, with another 64 points in 110 postseason contests. Lindell has missed the past five games due to a lower-body injury. Gulutzan mentioned, at the time, that the veteran blueliner suffered the injury when he blocked a shot in a previous game. items.body: Broadcasting icon's legendary calls include 'Golden Goal' for Canada at 2010 Olympics Chris Cuthbert grew up listening to Foster Hewitt and never imagined he would one day be receiving the Hockey Hall of Fame media award named after the legendary Canadian broadcaster. Cuthbert, this year's recipient of the Foster Hewitt Memorial Award for his outstanding contribution to broadcasting, will be honored at the Hockey Hall of Fame media luncheon in Toronto on Nov. 9. "It's overwhelming and it's the ultimate honor for an NHL broadcaster for sure," the 69-year-old told NHL.com. "I may be one of the last of the recipients who grew up listening to Foster Hewitt. He was the first guy to set the dream in motion. I'd go to bed at night with Foster Hewitt on the radio under the pillow listening to him." Cuthbert has become a Canadian broadcasting icon in his own right as the play-by-play voice for a generation of hockey fans. His call of Sidney Crosby 's overtime winner against the United States at the 2010 Vancouver Olympics has been compared to that of Hewitt's in Game 8 of the 1972 Summit Series when Paul Henderson scored the winning goal for Canada against the Soviet Union. Cuthbert was 15 when Hewitt famously exclaimed, "Here's a shot, Henderson made a wild stab for it and fell. Here's another shot, right in front, they score! Henderson has scored for Canada!" More than 37 years later, Cuthbert had a famous line of his own: "Crosby scores! Sidney Crosby, the golden goal and Canada has a once-in-a-lifetime Olympic gold!" Like Hewitt's famous call, Canadian hockey fans remember where they were listening to Cuthbert in the gold medal final. items.body: SUNRISE, Fla. — Anton Lundell had a hat trick, Seth Jones capped a record-setting month with a goal and two assists, and the Florida Panthers topped the reeling Winnipeg Jets 5-2 on Friday night for their sixth win in eight games. Jones finished October with 18 points — two goals and 16 assists — to break the record for most points by a Florida defenseman in any month. Keith Yandle had 17 points for the Panthers in March 2018. Kyle Connor had his team-best 11th goal for Winnipeg, which dropped both ends of a home-and-home with Florida this week and is winless in its last eight games — going 0-6-2 in that span. Morgan Barron had his first goal of the season midway through the third to get the Jets to 3-2, but Lundell's second of the night restored Florida's two-goal edge. Lundell finished off the hat trick — Florida's fifth already this season — with an empty-netter with 1:39 left. Akira Schmid stopped 22 shots for Florida, which remains without standout forwards Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand because of injuries. Both resumed skating this week; Marchand could be back in about three weeks and Barkov in about four, Panthers coach Paul Maurice said. Florida's Bokondji Imama and Winnipeg's Tyrel Bauer brawled just 2:04 into the game, a reenactment of sorts of their still-talked-about fight in the AHL in 2024. They went at it for more than a minute Friday and — similar to what happened at the end of their fight two years ago — shared a respectful nod toward the other when it was over. The Panthers entered Friday having played only three home games this season, the fewest in the NHL. More than half the league had logged at least seven home games going into the day.

items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” After a thorough examination of all available replays, there was no conclusive evidence that the puck shot by Florida’s Dmitry Kulikov at 12:03 (7:57 elapsed time) was deflected before going out of play . Therefore, the call on the ice stands. The decision was made in accordance with Rule 38.2 (d) which states, in part, that a team may request a Coach’s Challenge “When a minor penalty for delaying the game has been assessed under Rule 63.2 (iii) for shooting or batting the puck out of play from the defending zone. This will only apply to delay of game penalties when the shot/batted puck is determined to have subsequently deflected off a player, stick, glass or boards, etc., and not a judgment call.” Therefore, an additional minor penalty was assessed to Florida (in addition to the existing delay of game penalty).

items.body: Register Login Ducks Assign Nikita Klepov To OHL By Brennan McClain | at October 30, 2026 3:32 pm According to a team announcement , the Anaheim Ducks have returned forward Nikita Klepov to the OHL’s Saginaw Spirit. Klepov will remain with the Spirit through the end of the 2026-27 campaign and attempt to crack Anaheim’s roster next season. Because he didn’t reach the 10-game mark, or even come close, the Ducks can now slide Klepov’s entry-level contract despite him making his NHL debut. Klepov finishes his first four NHL contests going scoreless with a -2 rating, averaging 13:03 of ice time per game. On the one hand, it’s a smart move by Anaheim; even though Klepov had five more games of eligibility, the recent 15th overall pick should get more playing time. Now, Klepov can pick up where he left off with Saginaw. He scored 37 goals and 97 points in 67 games for the Spirit last season. Unfortunately for Saginaw, the Kitchener Rangers swept them in the 2026 OHL Playoffs conference quarterfinals. On the other hand, the Ducks may have missed the mark by signing Klepov to his entry-level contract so early. Before signing his first professional contract, Klepov was committed to play at Michigan State University for the 2026-27 campaign. However, since he signed a professional deal, he was no longer eligible for the NCAA. Instead, Klepov returns to a level he has already dominated after making four NHL appearances. If the Ducks weren’t planning to give him more opportunity, it would have been wiser to have him remain without a contract so he could play for the Spartans.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Colorado Avalanche head coach Jared Bednar announced on Friday that defenseman Josh Manson is going to about miss eight weeks due to an ankle injury. The injury occurred late in the first period of Wednesday’s 5-2 win over the New Jersey Devils after taking a weird hit. He struggled to get off the ice and had to be helped down the tunnel, and did not return to the game after that. The Avalanche confirmed his departure at the start of the third period. The Avalanche also haven’t announced a stint on injured reserve for Manson yet, but it wouldn’t be surprising if that happens sometime down the road. Manson joins Zachary L’Heureux on the Avalanche’s injury list, with L’Heureux out on a day-to-day basis with a lower-body injury. Manson has had a solid start to the season with one goal and three assists for four points in 13 games . That puts him on pace for his usual production in the 20-30 point range. While no lineup has been confirmed for Saturday’s game against the Calgary Flames , Noah Juulsen is the only other defenseman on the Avalanche roster who didn’t play on Wednesday, and will likely draw into the lineup on the third pairing. items.summary: Suddenly, the Oilers can win games with their defensive structure. And like the guy or not, there is a two-word answer for all of it: Mike Babcock. Sportsnet’s Mark Spector has more.
items.body: EAST MEADOW, N.Y. — Don’t look now, but the Edmonton Oilers lead the National Hockey League in rush chances against, and rank 25th in rush chances for. Connor McDavid played just 18:50 last game. Tristan Jarry had a shutout. And like the guy or not, there is a two-word answer for all of it: Mike Babcock. “You're getting called out on whatever you're not doing right to help the team win,” Leon Draisaitl said on Friday. That is exactly what McDavid was talking about back in June, when he, Zach Hyman and Draisaitl took a very active role in the Babcock hire. “It's time to have that happen in Edmonton,” McDavid said that day. “I’m excited about that challenge to be pushed by a coach, because it's been a really long time in Edmonton.” Today, the puck-possession Oilers rank second in the NHL in dump-in rate. They also rank second in puck battles won. “It's a simple game and (it is) determined by effort,” Babcock explained. “But if you have effort and you don't have structure, you're not playing together. You've got to arrive as five everywhere; you've got to play together. items.body: One full month of NHL action is behind us. With more than five months of regular-season play still ahead of us, there is still so much that can happen. What we think we may know about the season less than 20 per cent of the way in could change drastically by April — or, some early signs could stick and become season-long narratives. At this one-month touchpoint, we take a look around the league at some key early takeaways: At least three teams from the Atlantic — and maybe four! — will finish with crushing disappointment We knew this would be a competitive division, but this start has been wild. items.body: Register Login Assessing Elias Pettersson’s Potential Trade Value By Josh Cybulski | at October 30, 2026 1:00 pm It might seem crazy, but we are moving into a world where Vancouver Canucks forward Elias Pettersson might have meaningful trade value. Not just a bit of value, but potentially a decent amount if he keeps producing at the rate he has through 14 games this year. So far this year, the 27-year-old has notched four goals and 11 assists and is starting to look more like the player who signed an eight-year, $92.8MM contract extension in March 2024. That deal, which included $47MM in signing bonuses, looked unmovable and buyout-proof just 12 months ago, but with his hot start and an exploding salary cap, Pettersson could become a bit of a bargain. Now, 14 games at a point-per-game pace doesn’t automatically make Pettersson a Hart Trophy contender or even a top 25 scorer in the NHL. But if he can return to a 70+ point pace, he and his contract could have value in the new NHL economy, where some players are getting deals north of $20MM annually. If it seems crazy, that’s because it is. This past summer rewrote the NHL salary landscape, and it appears player salaries could keep trending upward. However, that’s not certain, which could create urgency for the Canucks to trade Pettersson if/when he has value. Yet teams could remain hesitant to make the move for Pettersson given his track record over the last few years. Teams could also proceed with caution because there are cautionary tales of teams acquiring players who had righted their play after a long track record of inconsistency, only to get the old, inconsistent version of the player rather than the improved one. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled on Friday that Russia must be eligible to return to ice hockey world championships, and hockey's governing bodies have responded. The ruling has the chance to impact Russian participation in five upcoming international events, with the upcoming IIHF World Junior Championships being first to commence on Dec. 26 in Edmonton and Red Deer, Alta. later this year. The IIHF responded to the news Friday morning, expressing its "disappointment with the decision." However, the IIHF will ultimately act in accordance with the CAS's ruling. While the Ukrainian hockey federation stated it respects the authority and status of the CAS, they align with the IIHF in its disagreement. "We express deep indignation at such a decision made in the conditions of a full-scale war. The threats that became the basis for the suspension of Russian teams in 2022 have not disappeared, but on the contrary, have only intensified." "In particular, on the night of October 18-19, another ice arena in Ukraine was damaged by a Russian missile strike, the twelfth since the Russian teams were suspended. items.title: Flames goaltender Devin Cooley week-to-week with lower-body injury
items.summary: The Calgary Flames will be without Devin Cooley for a while.
items.body: The team placed the goaltender on injured reserve Friday with a lower-body injury after he was forced to exit Wednesday's game against the Edmonton Oilers. Head coach Ryan Huska told reporters that Cooley will be week-to-week. Oilers forward Colton Dach crashed into Cooley with 12 seconds remaining in the opening 20 minutes and received a two-minute penalty for goaltender interference. Cooley remained in for the final 12 seconds but was not on the bench to start the second. He was then ruled out for the remainder of the game with a lower-body injury, the team announced. The 29-year-old had allowed just six goals on 133 shots over his previous four games entering Wednesday's game, good for a .955 save percentage. With Cooley out, Dustin Wolf is set to start the Flames' game against the Seattle Kraken Friday night (Sportsnet West, Sportsnet+, 8 p.m. ET / 6 p.m. MT). It will mark his first start since Oct. 15. Meanwhile, Arsenii Sergeev will serve as Wolf's backup after being recalled from the AHL's Calgary Wranglers. Forward William Stromgren was also recalled Friday from the Wranglers. In other injury news, Huska said Brennan Othmann is day-to-day with an upper-body injury, while Connor Zary has undergone knee surgery and is now considered week-to-week.

items.title: Senators’ Hodgson to have hearing for boarding, charging Kings’ Clarke
items.summary: Hodgson has no suspension history in the NHL, but was fined for boarding in the 2025 preseason.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The NHL Department of Player Safety announced on Friday that Ottawa Senators winger Hayden Hodgson will have a hearing for boarding and charging Los Angeles Kings defenseman Brandt Clarke during the Sens’ 6-5 overtime loss on Thursday. The infraction occurred midway during the second period of the game. As the Senators were dumping the puck into the Kings’ zone on an offensive rush, Clarke skated towards the boards in an attempt to make a play on the puck and regain possession. In doing so, he turned towards the boards, which opened the door for Hodgson to hit him from behind. In addition to the boarding, Hodgson also began to build up momentum for the hit from the top of the faceoff circle, a clear charging infraction on the play. As a result of the hit, Hodgson received a five-minute major penalty for boarding, as well as a 10-minute misconduct, and was ejected from the game. Kings’ center Erik Haula immediately responded to the hit and stuck up for Clarke by going after Hodgson, which resulted in a two-minute minor penalty for the Kings as well. Los Angeles also burned Hodgson and the Senators on the ensuing power play, as Artemi Panarin scored to give them a 5-1 lead, one they would blow in the third period before ultimately winning the game in overtime. Also as a result of the hit, the Kings announced that Clarke was ruled out for the rest of the game with an upper-body injury.
